effect: The genome is copied into joined sister chromatids, and the goal now is to separate two living cells.
reaction: The before-and-after distinction between copied DNA and still-joined chromosomes is useful.
reason: Use the spindle to separate the chromosome copies; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The spindle will help move sister chromatids toward opposite poles, preparing the cell for division.

effect: The chromosome sets are at opposite poles with new nuclear envelopes, but the cytoplasm remains continuous.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and cell separation is clear.
reason: Use the contractile ring to divide the cell; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The ring will narrow the cell's equator and separate it into two daughter cells.

effect: The ring completed cell separation, producing two living descendants and completing the chapter.
reaction: The furrowing sequence clearly distinguishes cell division from chromosome separation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Copying the genome was most worthwhile: the planned before-and-after inset distinguishes doubled DNA from still-joined sister chromatids.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first two fittings felt repetitive; they showed parts being added without much immediate explanation of growth.

surprise.text: The chromosome sets separated and new nuclear envelopes formed while the cytoplasm remained continuous, making the need for a separate division step clear.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though fitting proteins directly into the cell simplified cytoplasm growth without explaining the connection in much detail.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the unspecialized descendants supply different branches of the model; that prospect is more compelling than the repetitive early fittings.
